contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Wenfei Han and colleagues; the cited author evidence lists Melanie M Kaelberer as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: A Neural Circuit for Gut-Induced Reward.
sources.supports: The paper reports a neural circuit for gut-induced reward and lists Melanie M. Kaelberer as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Gut sensor-cell mechanism for sugar preference over sweetener
contributions.summary: Showed that CCK-labeled duodenal neuropod cells distinguish nutritive sugar from sweetener and are required for behavioral preference for sugar over noncaloric sweetener.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Kelly L Buchanan and colleagues; the cited author evidence lists M Maya Kaelberer as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: The preference for sugar over sweetener depends on a gut sensor cell.
sources.supports: The paper reports gut sensor-cell control of sugar preference and lists M. Maya Kaelberer as a coauthor.

identity.note: Imported roster identity; not independently established.

contribution_review.reason: Selected full-name matched C. elegans circuit and sensor/tool papers from the assigned evidence.

contributions.value: C. elegans local-search and dispersal navigation circuit
contributions.summary: Dissected sensory, interneuron, and motor-neuron roles in C. elegans exploratory navigation after food removal, linking defined neurons to reversals, omega turns, and dispersal.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Jesse M Gray and colleagues; the cited author evidence lists Cornelia I Bargmann as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: A circuit for navigation in Caenorhabditis elegans.
sources.supports: The paper reports a C. elegans navigation circuit and lists Cornelia I. Bargmann as a coauthor.

contributions.value: GCaMP3 calcium indicator for neural activity imaging across model organisms
contributions.summary: Co-developed and validated GCaMP3, showing improved fluorescence changes and detection of neural activity across worms, flies, and mice.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Lin Tian and colleagues; the cited author evidence lists Cornelia I Bargmann as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Imaging neural activity in worms, flies and mice with improved GCaMP calcium indicators.
sources.supports: The paper reports improved GCaMP calcium indicators and lists Cornelia I. Bargmann as a coauthor.

contributions.value: iGluSnFR fluorescent reporter for glutamate neurotransmission
contributions.summary: Co-developed iGluSnFR, an intensity-based fluorescent glutamate sensor validated in cultured neurons, brain slices, retina, and C. elegans for visualizing glutamate release.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Jonathan S Marvin and colleagues; the cited author evidence lists Cornelia I Bargmann as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: An optimized fluorescent probe for visualizing glutamate neurotransmission.
sources.supports: The paper reports an optimized glutamate neurotransmission probe and lists Cornelia I. Bargmann as a coauthor.

sources.title: Storing a Memory Involves Distant Parts of the Brain
sources.supports: HHMI describes mouse studies by Svoboda and members of his Janelia laboratory, including their work on ALM and short-term memory.

model_organisms.note: Explicit evidence of historical Janelia-lab mouse research. This is not a claim about the full organism inventory or current Allen-era personal-lab scope.

contributions.value: ALM persistent/preparatory activity for motor planning
contributions.summary: Linked movement-selective preparatory activity in mouse anterior lateral motor cortex to upcoming movement and its transformation into movement commands. Follow-up work showed recovery after unilateral disruption, supporting interacting hemispheres in robust motor planning.
contributions.attribution: Svoboda coauthored the 2015 study with Nuo Li, Tsai-Wen Chen, Zengcai V. Guo, and Charles R. Gerfen, and the 2016 study with Nuo Li, Kayvon Daie, and Shaul Druckmann. These are collaborative contributions, not sole-discovery claims.

sources.title: A motor cortex circuit for motor planning and movement.
sources.supports: The 2015 Li et al. paper names Svoboda as a coauthor and links mouse ALM preparatory activity, projection-neuron classes, and movement commands.

sources.title: Robust neuronal dynamics in premotor cortex during motor planning.
sources.supports: The 2016 Li, Daie, Svoboda, and Druckmann paper reports recovery of preparatory activity after unilateral disruption. Its contribution statement credits Li, Svoboda, and Druckmann with conception and experimental design.

contributions.note: The displayed year identifies the 2015 anchor; the second linked anchor is from 2016. This selected contribution family is not an exhaustive history or a priority claim for all motor-planning research.

contributions.value: ScanImage
contributions.summary: The original publication described open-source software for controlling laser-scanning microscopes and acquiring and processing images.
contributions.attribution: Svoboda coauthored the original ScanImage report with Thomas A. Pologruto and Bernardo L. Sabatini. Credit belongs to the collaborating authors and subsequent contributors, not to a sole inventor inferred from this profile.

sources.title: ScanImage: Flexible software for operating laser scanning microscopes.
sources.supports: The 2003 Pologruto, Sabatini, and Svoboda publication describes ScanImage and its laser-scanning microscopy software role.

contributions.note: A career-wide tool contribution predating the 2016-2025 count window. Citing it here does not add it to the publication tally.

sources.supports: HHMI describes mouse studies by Svoboda and members of his Janelia laboratory, including their work on ALM and short-term memory.

contributions.value: ALM persistent/preparatory activity for motor planning
contributions.summary: Linked movement-selective preparatory activity in mouse anterior lateral motor cortex to upcoming movement and its transformation into movement commands. Follow-up work showed recovery after unilateral disruption, supporting interacting hemispheres in robust motor planning.
contributions.attribution: Svoboda coauthored the 2015 study with Nuo Li, Tsai-Wen Chen, Zengcai V. Guo, and Charles R. Gerfen, and the 2016 study with Nuo Li, Kayvon Daie, and Shaul Druckmann. These are collaborative contributions, not sole-discovery claims.

sources.title: A motor cortex circuit for motor planning and movement.
sources.supports: The 2015 Li et al. paper names Svoboda as a coauthor and links mouse ALM preparatory activity, projection-neuron classes, and movement commands.

sources.title: Robust neuronal dynamics in premotor cortex during motor planning.
sources.supports: The 2016 Li, Daie, Svoboda, and Druckmann paper reports recovery of preparatory activity after unilateral disruption. Its contribution statement credits Li, Svoboda, and Druckmann with conception and experimental design.

contributions.note: The displayed year identifies the 2015 anchor; the second linked anchor is from 2016. This selected contribution family is not an exhaustive history or a priority claim for all motor-planning research.

contributions.value: ScanImage
contributions.summary: The original publication described open-source software for controlling laser-scanning microscopes and acquiring and processing images.
contributions.attribution: Svoboda coauthored the original ScanImage report with Thomas A. Pologruto and Bernardo L. Sabatini. Credit belongs to the collaborating authors and subsequent contributors, not to a sole inventor inferred from this profile.

sources.title: ScanImage: Flexible software for operating laser scanning microscopes.
sources.supports: The 2003 Pologruto, Sabatini, and Svoboda publication describes ScanImage and its laser-scanning microscopy software role.

contributions.value: Millisecond optogenetic control of mammalian neural activity
contributions.summary: Adapted Channelrhodopsin-2 for temporally precise optical stimulation of mammalian neurons, demonstrating control of single-spike timing and excitatory or inhibitory synaptic transmission as a broadly useful neural perturbation tool.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Edward S Boyden and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Karl Deisseroth as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Millisecond-timescale, genetically targeted optical control of neural activity.
sources.supports: The paper reports Channelrhodopsin-2-based millisecond control of mammalian neuronal spiking and synaptic transmission and lists Karl Deisseroth as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Parvalbumin interneuron control of cortical gamma rhythms
contributions.summary: Used optogenetic modulation in mouse neocortex to show that parvalbumin interneurons can suppress or generate gamma-frequency rhythmicity and that gamma-frequency input modulation can improve signal transmission.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Vikaas S Sohal and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Karl Deisseroth as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Parvalbumin neurons and gamma rhythms enhance cortical circuit performance.
sources.supports: The paper reports bidirectional optogenetic tests of parvalbumin interneuron roles in gamma rhythms and lists Karl Deisseroth as a coauthor.

contributions.value: CLARITY intact-tissue molecular and structural imaging
contributions.summary: Introduced CLARITY, transforming intact tissue into a transparent, macromolecule-permeable hydrogel hybrid that enabled three-dimensional imaging and molecular labeling across mouse brain and clinical tissue samples.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Kwanghun Chung and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Karl Deisseroth as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Structural and molecular interrogation of intact biological systems.
sources.supports: The paper describes CLARITY for intact-tissue structural and molecular interrogation and lists Karl Deisseroth as a coauthor.

contributions.value: GCaMP3 calcium indicator for neural activity imaging
contributions.summary: Improved GCaMP2 into GCaMP3 with stronger baseline fluorescence, dynamic range, calcium affinity, and in vivo performance across worms, flies, and mice, enabling more sensitive neural activity imaging.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Lin Tian and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Loren L Looger as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Imaging neural activity in worms, flies and mice with improved GCaMP calcium indicators.
sources.supports: The paper reports development and cross-species testing of GCaMP3 and lists Loren L. Looger as a coauthor.

contributions.value: GCaMP6 ultrasensitive fluorescent calcium sensors
contributions.summary: Developed GCaMP6 sensors through mutagenesis and neuron-based screening, demonstrating single-action-potential detection and tuned synaptic calcium transients in multiple model systems including mouse visual cortex.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Tsai-Wen Chen and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Loren L Looger as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Ultrasensitive fluorescent proteins for imaging neuronal activity.

contributions.value: rAAV2-retro access to projection neurons
contributions.summary: Engineered rAAV2-retro by in vivo directed evolution to provide robust retrograde access to projection neurons, supporting sensor or effector expression for functional circuit interrogation and genome editing in targeted populations.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with D Gowanlock R Tervo and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Loren L Looger as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: A Designer AAV Variant Permits Efficient Retrograde Access to Projection Neurons.

contributions.value: TRPA1 transduction of irritants and inflammatory pain signals
contributions.summary: Identified TRPA1/ANKTM1 as a sensory-neuron target for pungent irritants and showed in mutant mice that TRPA1 mediates responses to mustard oil, garlic-derived compounds, environmental irritants, and bradykinin-evoked pain hypersensitivity.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Sven-Eric Jordt, Diana M Bautista, and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Diana M Bautista as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: TRPA1 mediates the inflammatory actions of environmental irritants and proalgesic agents.

contributions.value: TRPM8 as a principal detector of environmental cold
contributions.summary: Showed that TRPM8-deficient sensory neurons, nerve fibers, and mice have strongly diminished cold responses, establishing TRPM8 as a predominant peripheral detector across a broad range of cool temperatures.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Diana M Bautista and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Diana M Bautista as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: The menthol receptor TRPM8 is the principal detector of environmental cold.

contributions.value: Epithelial TSLP activation of sensory neurons to drive itch
contributions.summary: Showed that calcium-dependent TSLP release from keratinocytes can directly activate a subset of TRPA1-positive cutaneous sensory neurons, linking epithelial cytokine signaling to itch behaviors in atopic dermatitis models.

contributions.value: Bat grid cells without continuous theta oscillations
contributions.summary: Recorded medial entorhinal grid cells in Egyptian fruit bats and found grid-like spatial firing without continuous theta-band oscillations, challenging oscillatory-interference explanations requiring theta rhythmicity.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Michael M Yartsev and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Michael M Yartsev as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

contributions.value: Three-dimensional hippocampal place coding in flying bats
contributions.summary: Used wireless recordings in freely flying bats to show that hippocampal place cells encode confined three-dimensional volumes with similar resolution across axes, supporting a volumetric spatial representation.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Michael M Yartsev and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Michael M Yartsev as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Representation of three-dimensional space in the hippocampus of flying bats.

contributions.summary: IDE-deficient mice showed reduced degradation of amyloid beta in brain fractions and insulin in liver, with increased endogenous cerebral amyloid beta and metabolic abnormalities, linking IDE hypofunction to AD- and diabetes-relevant biology.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Wesley Farris, Stefan Mansourian, Yang Chang and colleagues; the primary paper lists Rudolph E. Tanzi as a coauthor.

sources.title: Insulin-degrading enzyme regulates the levels of insulin, amyloid beta-protein, and the beta-amyloid precursor protein intracellular domain in vivo.

contributions.value: 3D human neural culture model of Alzheimer pathology
contributions.summary: Human neural stem-cell-derived 3D cultures carrying familial AD mutations developed extracellular amyloid deposits and tau pathology in one system; secretase inhibition reduced both amyloid pathology and downstream tauopathy.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Se Hoon Choi, Young Hye Kim, Matthias Hebisch and colleagues; the primary paper lists Rudolph E. Tanzi as a coauthor.

sources.title: A three-dimensional human neural cell culture model of Alzheimer's disease.
sources.supports: Supports the 3D Alzheimer culture model and Tanzi's authorship.

contributions.value: Amyloid beta antimicrobial activity
contributions.summary: The study reported antimicrobial activity of amyloid beta against multiple clinically relevant microorganisms and linked increased antimicrobial action in AD brain homogenates to amyloid beta levels and antibody depletion.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Stephanie J. Soscia, James E. Kirby, Kevin J. Washicosky and colleagues; the primary paper lists Rudolph E. Tanzi as a coauthor.

sources.title: The Alzheimer's disease-associated amyloid beta-protein is an antimicrobial peptide.
sources.supports: Supports the amyloid beta antimicrobial finding and Tanzi's authorship.

sources.title: Identification of a molecular signaling network that regulates a cellular necrotic cell death pathway.

contributions.value: Salubrinal inhibition of eIF2α dephosphorylation

sources.title: A selective inhibitor of eIF2alpha dephosphorylation protects cells from ER stress.

sources.title: Endocannabinoids control the induction of cerebellar LTD.

sources.title: KIF1A/UNC-104 Transports ATG-9 to Regulate Neurodevelopment and Autophagy at Synapses.

sources.title: Molecular evolution of the insect chemoreceptor gene superfamily in Drosophila melanogaster.

sources.title: Leptin signaling in astrocytes regulates hypothalamic neuronal circuits and feeding.

contributions.summary: In people with chronic stroke, reduced responsiveness and activity-dependent modulation of motor-cortical networks were associated with impaired propulsive walking mechanics. The findings connect neural network flexibility with particular biomechanical deficits rather than demonstrating a treatment effect.
contributions.attribution: Jacqueline A. Palmer is first author, with T. M. Kesar, S. L. Wolf and M. R. Borich as coauthors.

sources.title: Motor Cortical Network Flexibility is Associated With Biomechanical Walking Impairment in Chronic Stroke.
sources.supports: Supports the association between cortical network flexibility and walking impairment and identifies Jacqueline A Palmer as first author.

contributions.note: Association study; do not infer that changing the measured network property necessarily improves walking.

contributions.value: Preliminary exercise-related changes in poststroke inhibitory control
contributions.summary: A small preliminary study in people with chronic stroke reported improved response inhibition after aerobic exercise training, with performance related to cortical response timing. The findings suggest a selective inhibitory-control effect but do not establish durable clinical benefit.
contributions.attribution: Jacqueline A. Palmer is first author, with Whitaker, Payne, Bartsch, Reisman, Boyne and Billinger as coauthors.

sources.title: Aerobic Exercise Improves Cortical Inhibitory Function After Stroke: A Preliminary Investigation.
sources.supports: Supports the preliminary exercise and inhibitory-control findings and identifies Jacqueline A Palmer as first author.

contributions.note: Journal publication year 2024; first online 2023-07-10. Preliminary small-sample findings, not definitive treatment efficacy.

contributions.value: SCN3A channel function in prenatal cortical development
contributions.summary: Human genetic and developmental analyses linked SCN3A variants with abnormal cortical folding and oral-motor difficulties. Complementary model-system evidence supported a role for the sodium channel in prenatal cortical development, beyond its better-known function in mature excitable cells.
contributions.attribution: Richard S. Smith is first author; the collaborative author list includes Christopher A. Walsh and Maria K. Lehtinen as the final two authors.

contributions.value: Neural prioritization of hunger over inflammatory pain
contributions.summary: The study linked hunger-driven suppression of inflammatory pain to signaling between hypothalamic hunger neurons and the parabrachial nucleus. The effect spared acute nociceptive responses, distinguishing competing-need modulation from a uniform reduction in pain responses.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored by first author Amber L. Alhadeff, last author J. Nicholas Betley, and colleagues; no sole-discovery or mentorship claim is inferred.

contributions.note: Preclinical circuit findings, not an established clinical analgesic treatment.

contributions.value: Distinct neural pathways for sustained-pain coping
